newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures take breather after rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures take breather after rally.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures fluctuated but ended mostly flat on Friday in further consolidation of recent sharp gains.
Prices reached the day's peaks early in the session on spill-over fund and trade buying. But buyers disappeared in the afternoon and prices were also knocked lower by profit-takers.
"I think the market is trying to consolidate around this level," said one.
"It had seen a big rise in heavy volume in the last two days...it needs to catch its breath really," he added.
Most-active March rose to a high of $1,330 a tonne before finishing the day at $1,320, the same as Thursday's finish.
The day's low was $1,309, well above its major support at $1,293..
The March position scored gains of nearly 11 percent in the past three days on fund-backed short-covering and stop loss buying. Traders said the fund buying was nearly at its end.
Technically, analysts said a close above $1,324 basis March on Friday would suggest further gains were on the cards.
A major upside goal is seen at $1,399 but analyst Darren Gurner at Sucden said there was also some nearby resistance around $1,340 and $1,350.
Volume reached 8,558 lots, down from over 10,000 lots a day in the last two days.
The options market saw another hectic day on Friday, with turnover reaching 2,097 lots. Options traders said volume centred on March $1,400/May $1,400 call spread.
Futures traders said the market's immediate direction would hinged partly on origin sellers.
Producers stepped back from the market following the rally, trying to see how far the market could get.
"If we don't see any more movements on the upside next week, the origins will be back again," one said.
